Q: How can I improve search time A:

It is not clear whether you need to search for a single attribute value (or range) or a collection of attribute values (or ranges). I will assume the latter.

Let assume you have passed the search criteria into your stored procedure or table-returning function and have populated the following search criteria table variable:

DECLARE @SearchCriteria TABLE (
    CriteriaID INT IDENTITY(1,1),
    AttributeName NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Value NVARCHAR(500) NOT NULL, -- Single or lower Text/Number/Date/Boolean value
    UpperValue NVARCHAR(500)      -- Non-null for Number or Date range
);

(A table variable behaves very much like a #temp table with local scope.)

Because your search involves multiple types and potentially a combination of discrete values and ranges, I believe it is best to split the search up into several subqueries that are UNION'd together. Conditions in each subquery will shortcut the results when that subquery does not apply to a given data type or value/range criteria type. This way, only one of the subqueries will actively search for results for any given criteria row.

To select only those products that match all criteria conditions, you can count the matches and only return products where the match count equals the criteria count.

Such a query could look something like:

DECLARE @CriteriaCount INT = (
    SELECT COUNT(*)
    FROM @SearchCriteria
);

DECLARE @MatchingProducts TABLE (
    ProductID INT
);

INSERT INTO @MatchingProducts
SELECT A.ProductId
FROM @SearchCriteria SC
JOIN ProductAttributes PA
    ON PA.AttributeName = SC.AttributeName
CROSS APPLY (
    -- Text
    SELECT PAV.ProductID
    FROM ProductAttributeValues PAV
    WHERE PA.AttributeType = 1 -- Text
    AND PAV.AttributeID = PA.ID
    AND PAV.TextValue = SC.Value

    UNION ALL

    -- Number (value)
    SELECT PAV.ProductID
    FROM ProductAttributeValues PAV
    WHERE PA.AttributeType = 2 -- Number
    AND SC.UpperValue IS NULL  -- Single value
    AND PAV.AttributeID = PA.ID
    AND PAV.NumberValue = TRY_CAST(SC.Value AS DECIMAL(18,2))

    UNION ALL

    -- Number (range)
    SELECT PAV.ProductID
    FROM ProductAttributeValues PAV
    WHERE PA.AttributeType = 2     -- Number
    AND SC.UpperValue IS NOT NULL  -- Range
    AND PAV.AttributeID = PA.ID
    AND PAV.NumberValue >= TRY_CAST(SC.Value AS DECIMAL(18,2))
    AND PAV.NumberValue <= TRY_CAST(SC.UpperValue AS DECIMAL(18,2))

    --UNION ALL
    -- ... similar for date value, date range, and boolean value
) A
GROUP BY A.ProductId
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT SC.CriteriaID) = @CriteriaCount;

The GROUP BY together with the COUNT() check will effectively INTERSECT the results from each attribute value search.

Once you have the matching ProductID list, you can feed that into another query that applies any additional conditions and retrieves the required data for your results.

Q: C, structs and pointers - why does this work? A:

Why does this work? That's the beauty of Undefined Behavior, it's like a box of chocolates, you never know what you are going to get. Your program may appear to run fine or it may SegFault, it's a dice roll.

Since foo and bar contain pointers, those pointers must hold a valid memory address to which your code can write. There is no such valid memory provided in your code. The fact that it worked is -- undefined.

If you always ask, and answer, the question, "to what valid memory does each of my pointers point?", you will avoid access problems such as this. You can use malloc(), calloc() or realloc() to allocate storage, or you can simply provide valid automatic storage such as arrays, e.g.

  int a[5] = {0}, b[5] = {0};
  struct comb c = { .f = {a}, .b = {b} };

Whether you use dynamic memory allocation, or provide the address of an object with sufficient storage regardless of the storage type, the result is the same. Your pointers hold the address of memory you can validly read/write from and the execution of your program is defined.

Q: npm is broken, and I can not run any npm command A:

For Windows, delete folder node_modules from the path C:\Program Files\nodejs\node_modules.

Q: Re-throwing Python exception, which to catch? A:

There are several methods to resolve it:

1. Exception Chain

raise NewException("Explain why") from CatchedException

pattern. In particular, considering Python 3 and the example given by @BrenBarn I use following

def failure():
    raise ValueError("Real error")

try:
    failure()
except ValueError as ex:
    raise TypeError("Apology error") from ex

which yields

--------- ValueError----                                
Traceback (most recent call last) 
      4 try:
----> 5     failure()
      6 except ValueError as ex:

      1 def failure():
----> 2     raise ValueError("Real error")
      3 

ValueError: Real error

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

-----TypeError-----
Traceback (most recent call last) 
      5     failure()
      6 except ValueError as ex:
----> 7     raise TypeError("Apology error") from ex

TypeError: Apology error

2. Suppress Original Failure

You can also suppress the original exception context by raise the new exception from None. The code will change to

def failure():
    raise ValueError("Real error")

try:
    failure()
except ValueError as ex:
    raise TypeError("Apology error") from None

.. and it yields following output

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[2], line 7
      5     failure()
      6 except ValueError as ex:
----> 7     raise TypeError("Apology error") from None

TypeError: Apology error

3. Add Notes To Exception

You can also add explanation notes to original exception

def failure(i):
    raise ValueError(f"Real error in failure method.")

try:
    a = 3.1415
    failure(a)
except ValueError as ex:
    ex.add_note(f'The "{ex.args[0]}" happened with argument {a} when invoked from main script.')
    ex.add_note('Final note: bye')
    raise

which yields ...

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ValueError                                Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[14], line 6
      4 try:
      5     a = 3.1415
----> 6     failure(a)
      7 except ValueError as ex:
      8     ex.add_note(f'The "{ex.args[0]}" happened with argument {a} when invoked from main script.')

Cell In[14], line 2, in failure(i)
      1 def failure(i):
----> 2     raise ValueError(f"Real error in failure method.")

ValueError: Real error in failure method.
The "Real error in failure method." happened with argument 3.1415 when invoked from main script.
Final note: bye

Q: Split string before and after bracketed expressions and omit brackets from the results A:

You can split on braced expressions and retain the captured expression within the braces with PREG_SPLIT_DELIM_CAPTURE. Demo

var_export(
    preg_split(
        '#\[([^]]+)\]#',
        $str,
        0,
        PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY | PREG_SPLIT_DELIM_CAPTURE
    )
);

array (
  0 => '%%%%%%',
  1 => '%%%%',
  2 => '%%%%%%%%',
)

Pattern breakdown:

\[        # match a literal left brace
  (       # start capture grouo
   [^]]+  # match one or more non-right-braces
  )       # end capture group
\]        # match a literal right brace

The escaping slash before the literal right brace at the end of the pattern is not needed, but makes the pattern intention more explicit/obvious/consistent.

Q: Exclude hidden dot files with tar A:

Order matters with tar apparently!

While the command in the question didn't work, rearranging --exclude to be at the front did. Many of the guides I found online were either wrong in the example commands they gave or didn't specify, so I thought I would answer my own question when I figured it out.

tar --exclude=".*" -zcvf dist.tar.gz Foo/ Bar/ Buzz/

Q: Npm is not working after Yarn install (cannot find number-is-nan) A:

Try to use yarn to reinstall npm:

yarn global add npm
